sql.title: Query paid orders
sql.about: Filter orders using the real Spark SQL engine. The orders view is already registered.
sql.sql: SELECT order_id, total FROM orders WHERE status = 'paid' ORDER BY order_id;

sql.title: Group accounts by currency
sql.about: Group the same banking records with SQL or the DataFrame API.
sql.sql: SELECT currency, COUNT(*) AS count FROM accounts GROUP BY currency ORDER BY currency;

sql.title: Join employees and departments
sql.about: Inspect department membership, including employees without a matching department.
sql.sql: SELECT e.employee_id, e.department_id, d.department_name FROM employees e LEFT JOIN departments d ON e.department_id = d.department_id ORDER BY e.employee_id;

sql.title: Number employees within departments
sql.about: Use a Spark SQL window to number employees without changing the number of rows.
sql.sql: SELECT employee_id, department_id, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY department_id ORDER BY employee_id) AS position FROM employees ORDER BY employee_id;
sql.python:
from pyspark.sql import functions as F
from pyspark.sql.window import Window
result = employees.select('employee_id', 'department_id', F.row_number().over(Window.partitionBy('department_id').orderBy('employee_id')).alias('position')).orderBy('employee_id')

sql.title: Create and query a temporary view
sql.about: Both statements share one run. Running again starts from the original data.
sql.sql:
CREATE OR REPLACE TEMP VIEW paid_orders AS SELECT * FROM orders WHERE status = 'paid';
SELECT order_id, total FROM paid_orders ORDER BY order_id;

sql.title: Create a disposable reporting table
sql.about: Build a Parquet table in the private warehouse. It exists only during this run.
sql.sql:
CREATE TABLE account_counts USING parquet AS SELECT country, COUNT(*) AS count FROM accounts GROUP BY country;
SELECT * FROM account_counts ORDER BY country;

sql.title: Query a Parquet file
sql.about: Write a disposable Parquet table, then query its files in the same run.
sql.sql:
CREATE TABLE trip_counts USING parquet LOCATION '/tmp/work/trip_counts' AS SELECT pickup_zone_id, COUNT(*) AS count FROM trips GROUP BY pickup_zone_id;
SELECT * FROM parquet.`/tmp/work/trip_counts` ORDER BY pickup_zone_id;

sql.about: Create a private Delta table and update one region. Shared warehouses are read-only inputs.

warehouses.write.format('delta').mode('overwrite').saveAsTable('lab_warehouses')

compare.title: DataFrame API and Spark SQL
compare.about: Two ways to count orders by status. Equivalence checks every row and its multiplicity; the scratch workspace has no independent task oracle.
compare.b: result = spark.sql('SELECT status, COUNT(*) AS count FROM orders GROUP BY status')

compare.title: Keeping and removing duplicates
compare.about: The practice export has duplicate deliveries. Removing duplicates changes the result contract.

compare.title: Inner and left joins
compare.about: A left join retains unmatched transactions. Check missing account keys and nulls.

compare.title: Built-in function and Python UDF
compare.about: Both uppercase first names. Inspect the actual Python evaluation operator; timing is a separate experiment.
compare.a:
from pyspark.sql import functions as F
result = employees.select('employee_id', F.upper('first_name').alias('name'))
compare.b:
from pyspark.sql import functions as F
upper_name = F.udf(lambda x: x.upper() if x is not None else None, 'string')
result = employees.select('employee_id', upper_name('first_name').alias('name'))

compare.title: Repartition and coalesce
compare.about: Both preserve records. Their physical plans reveal different partition operations.

compare.title: Aggregation and window grain
compare.about: Aggregation returns one row per status. A window preserves the source grain, even if it repeats the same totals.
compare.b:
from pyspark.sql import functions as F
from pyspark.sql.window import Window
result = orders.select('status', F.count('*').over(Window.partitionBy('status')).alias('count'))
